thesis: ADT agreed on Oct 29, 2026 to be acquired by Thrive Holdings, backed by Josh Kushner's Thrive Capital, for $10.00 per share in cash. That is a 45.6% premium to the unaffected Oct 27 close, about $7.6B of equity value and $15.3B of enterprise value, with all financing from Apollo-managed funds and no financing condition. Closing is expected in Q1 2027, subject to stockholder and antitrust approval, and ADT may solicit competing offers through Nov 28. The stock rose about 33% today to $9.87 on 22x volume, about 1.3% below the deal price, so upside appears capped barring a topping bid. A March 2026 law-firm investigation over Q4 results has no filed claim identified.
invalidation: A topping bid above $10.00 during the go-shop period.

thesis: Iovance fell about 35.5% today to $9.55 on 3.8x volume after updated Phase 2 data for lifileucel in previously treated non-small cell lung cancer. The objective response rate was 24.6% across 69 patients and 59.1% in a 22-patient biomarker-selected subgroup, with commentary raising durability questions and the prospect of a narrower approval path. The company plans a new POSITILITY study arm in November and an FDA filing in 2027. The evidence is mixed: the subgroup signal is strong, but the broad-population data disappointed. A 2025 securities class action (N.D. Cal.) over the Amtagvi launch has no scheduled ruling identified.
invalidation: Durable responses in the biomarker-selected population and a clear regulatory path for the 2027 filing.

thesis: Bausch Health rose about 28% today to $8.885 on 15x volume, a 52-week high, extending the Oct 28 move after its Q3 2026 beat-and-raise. Revenue was $2.94B, adjusted EPS $1.77 against ~$1.27 expected, and full-year guidance was raised for a second straight quarter; coverage cites debt reduction topping $1B and a $50M buyback. The counter-cases are structural and unresolved, which caps this at medium. Debt is roughly $20B with liabilities exceeding assets. Xifaxan, about 85% of Salix revenue, faces a Medicare price change that hits Q4 and loss of exclusivity in 2028. This run found no going-concern language or scheduled legal ruling.
invalidation: Cash flow or debt reduction stalls, guidance is cut on the Xifaxan Medicare pricing change, or an adverse Xifaxan exclusivity development.

thesis: Glaukos rose about 33.6% today to $242.39 on 5.1x volume, a 52-week high, after its Q3 2026 report. Revenue of about $211M was up 58% year over year against ~$168M expected, non-GAAP EPS of $0.47 beat an expected loss, and 2026 net sales guidance was raised to $775-785M. Management also gave a preliminary 2027 revenue target of $1B, which it called highly preliminary. The catalyst is a confirmed, company-specific beat-and-raise, but this run retrieved no company release or filing for it and found no fundamental counter-case beyond valuation, so it caps at medium. This run found no 2026 lawsuit, investigation or restatement; past patent disputes were settled.
invalidation: Q4 results fall short of the raised guidance, or iDose/Epioxa adoption slows.

thesis: Fortrea fell about 10.6% today to $23.135 on 2.6x volume despite reporting Q3 2026 results that beat expectations: EPS of $0.28 against $0.22 and revenue of $691.5M against ~$671.6M. This run found no explanation for the drop, so the read is unresolved after a 41% 60-day run. A 2025 securities class action over the company's 2025 EBITDA targets remains ongoing with no scheduled ruling identified, and a November 2025 law-firm fiduciary investigation has no filed claim.
invalidation: A disclosed explanation for the selloff that leaves the beat intact, or Q4 results that confirm the trend.

thesis: Crocs reported Q3 2026 today (company press release). Adjusted EPS of $3.69 beat the ~$3.30 consensus, revenue of $1.04B topped ~$1.0B, Crocs brand revenue hit a third-quarter record of $873M (+4.4%), and full-year revenue guidance was raised for the third straight time to about +3% (from +1-2%). The stock rose about 25.5% to $150.25 on 4.8x volume, near its 52-week high. The strongest counter-case is HEYDUDE: the brand's prolonged decline underlies a pending securities class action (D. Del.). That doesn't change the read, because HEYDUDE returned to growth this quarter (+6.1% to $170M) in the company's own disclosed results. This run found no scheduled ruling in the class action and no restatement.
invalidation: HEYDUDE slips back into decline, Q4 results miss the raised outlook, or an adverse ruling in the HEYDUDE securities class action.

thesis: Instacart agreed on Oct 29, 2026 to be acquired by DoorDash for $65.00 per share (DoorDash 8-K), payable in cash, DoorDash stock or a mix, with stock capped at 25% of total consideration. That is a 26% premium to the Oct 22 close, and the board approved unanimously. Closing is expected only at the end of 2027 or early 2028, and the combination faces significant antitrust review. At $57.13 (down about 2.2% today on 4.5x volume), CART sits about 12% below the deal price, which suggests the market is pricing that regulatory risk and the long timeline. Upside appears capped at $65 while a regulatory block would expose it to a large drop. The FTC has an open civil investigative demand over the company's AI pricing tool; it follows a $60M Instacart+ settlement entered Dec 2025.
invalidation: Antitrust clearance arrives early, or a competing bid above $65.

thesis: Stagwell reported Q3 2026 today (8-K). Revenue rose 10% to $816M, short of ~$838M expected, while adjusted EPS of $0.34 beat ~$0.31. Digital Transformation net revenue grew 23% organically, and full-year guidance was raised to adjusted EBITDA of $490-540M and adjusted EPS of $1.07-1.21. The stock rose about 12.9% to $9.965 on 2.7x volume, near its 52-week high. In February 2024 the company disclosed errors in its 2022 financial statements and revised them, raising tax expense by about $18M. That accounting correction falls inside the 3-year window and flags governance history. A March 2026 law-firm fiduciary investigation has no filed claim.
invalidation: Q4 results miss the raised guidance, or a further accounting issue.

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 19). AVTR was little changed at $16.675, about 4% below its 52-week high, and this run found no new company disclosure since the Oct 28 Q3 report (8-K). That report showed net sales up 4.6% to $1,698.3M with 5.2% organic growth, adjusted EPS of $0.22, and raised 2026 organic growth, adjusted EPS and free-cash-flow guidance. The counter-cases from the prior thesis remain open. Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS still declined year over year, so margins have not followed sales, and the motion to dismiss the securities class action has no ruling date. This stays medium.
invalidation: Q4 results fall short of the raised guidance, an adverse class-action ruling, or a close back below the 20-day average.

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 20). CLF rose about 2.4% today to $14.28, above the ~$12.12 pre-report level, and this run found no new company disclosure. The thesis rests on the Oct 19 Q3 report: adjusted EBITDA of $612M against $575M guidance, Q4 guided to about $715M, and 2027 guided above $4B. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open. The outlook depends on contract changes and steel-price forecasts, and the Hamilton (Stelco) layoffs confirmed Oct 21 point to tariff pressure on the Canadian unit. This stays medium.
invalidation: Steel prices or contract pricing weaken enough to put the Q4/2027 EBITDA outlook at risk, a confirmed material Stelco shutdown or forced sale, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$12.12).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22). ROIV rose about 1.1% to $37.51, above its ~$34.92 pre-announcement level, and this run found no new company disclosure. The thesis rests on the Oct 21-22 CLARITY Phase 3 results for brepocitinib (branded LISRAYA by Priovant) in non-infectious uveitis, which showed longer time to treatment failure and higher steroid-free quiescence rates than placebo; the drug is already approved for dermatomyositis. The counter-case named in the prior thesis remains open: the uveitis indication is not yet approved and the sNDA is not planned until 1H 2027. Fiscal Q2 results on Nov 9 are the next scheduled event. This stays medium.
invalidation: Full CLARITY data or FDA feedback reveal a safety or efficacy problem, or a close back below the pre-announcement level (~$34.92).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 26). RNG fell about 2.9% to $83.66, still above the ~$79.42 pre-report level, and this run found no new company disclosure. The thesis rests on the Oct 22 Q3 2026 report (8-K). Revenue rose 5.9% to $676M, above the $664-670M guidance, and the non-GAAP operating margin reached 24.7%, up about 190bp. Full-year guidance was raised to $2.650-2.657B in revenue, $5.07-5.12 in non-GAAP EPS and $620-630M in free cash flow. ARR from customers using a paid AI product doubled to nearly 15% of the total. The strongest counter-case is competitive: growth is only about 6% in a crowded cloud-communications market. That doesn't change the read, because the beat, the margin expansion and the raised EPS and free-cash-flow guidance all come from the company's own disclosed results at that growth rate. This is the counter-case named and resolved in the prior thesis, and no new fact reopens it. A January 2026 law-firm investigation notice has no filed claim, the 10-Q shows no material proceeding, and the next earnings report is about four months away (Feb 2027).
invalidation: Q4 revenue or margin falls short of the raised guidance, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$79.42).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 28). Centene rose about 2.3% today to $68.625, closing back above its ~$68.03 pre-report level, and this run found no new company disclosure. The thesis rests on the Oct 27 Q3 report (8-K): adjusted EPS of $0.58 against a consensus near $0.07-0.10, full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to above $5.20, and Medicare Advantage now expected to break even in 2026, a year early. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open and cap this at medium. Medicaid margins are pressured (93.6% benefits ratio), with management expecting membership declines and acuity shifts to slow recovery through 2027. The quarter's GAAP loss of $0.14 per share is not attributed to a specific charge. A securities class action (Lunstrum v. Centene, S.D.N.Y.) has no scheduled ruling identified.
invalidation: Medicaid cost trends worsen enough to put the raised guidance at risk, or the stock falls back below the pre-report level (~$68.03).
